args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploying checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Verified after rollback: all regions are on v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying, and review why it was promoted after the unhealthy staging RC.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened SEV2 incident INC-0001. The service is healthy again.

- **Problem:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an 18% error rate. Its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had also been unhealthy in staging.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. Change-manager approval wasn't needed because v2.3.0 has run healthy in production before.
- **Check after rollback:** all three regions are on v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback and the check above, and it paged the on-call engineer. It lists two follow-ups: find the root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying it, and find out why it was released after its release candidate failed in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
